content.text: {"architecturalPlan":{"scaleRationale":"This targeted revision retains the established expansive waterfront residence rather than inflating its programme. The meaningful change is the completion of the already-modelled upper west suite as a genuine private outdoor room: a compact elevated terrace makes the taller west anchor useful, improves its proportion against the central salon, and avoids adding unjustified new amenities or detached buildings.","arrivalAndCirculation":"Landward arrival remains through the limestone court, framed portal and recessed bronze entrance beneath the dedicated timber canopy. The entrance leads into the tall central salon. The principal oceanward route is now physically resolved by replacing the salon’s central glazed bay with a full-height bronze terrace door, providing direct movement from the salon to the covered ocean terrace, pool court and pavilion. The elevated west-suite terrace is connected to its existing ocean-side upper-suite door; vertical circulation to that upper suite remains unmodelled.","volumeHierarchy":"The composition is preserved as a tall central living salon, a more private low east wing, and a distinct recessed two-storey west anchor. The new upper west terrace extends the upper suite toward the water without enlarging the enclosed mass, strengthening the intended stepped primary-secondary hierarchy. The central salon remains the principal communal volume, with the lateral wings subordinate and the pool pavilion detached beyond the terrace.","relationshipsAndViews":"Three ocean-facing salon bays remain legible, but the centre bay is now an operable threshold rather than an inaccessible glazed opening. The flanking glazed bays retain framed ocean views. The deep covered terrace remains the principal shared outdoor room; new lateral bronze slat screens make its exposed edges more private and reduce lateral glare while preserving the forward outlook. The upper west terrace is enclosed by transparent guards on its exposed edges and retains the existing ocean-facing suite door.","roofFacadeAndMaterials":"The stepped flat-roof composition is retained: the highest limestone salon roof reads as the communal centre, while the smaller upper-west roof remains set back over the suite. Ivory enclosure, limestone floor and roof edges, timber canopies, and selective bronze doors/screens are consolidated into a restrained tropical palette. the new terrace projects beyond the recessed upper roof as an intentionally open, guarded outdoor room.","elementIds":["salon-roof","west-upper-roof","west-upper-terrace-deck","west-upper-terrace-rail"],"limitation":"The open upper terrace is not roof-sheltered; waterproofing, drainage, guard compliance, and engineering are not verified."},{"disposition":"constructed","knowledgeId":"waterfront-estate","decision":"Prioritized direct communal movement from the salon to the covered view terrace and screened its lateral edges while retaining the existing axial pool and pavilion sequence.","elementIds":["salon-view-center","salon-ocean-door","ocean-terrace","terrace-screen-west","terrace-screen-east","pool-water","ocean-pavilion"],"limitation":"Ocean orientation, shoreline location, flood elevation, legal setbacks, and marine conditions remain unverified assumptions."}]},"name":"Maison des Alizés","summary":"Targeted development pass preserving the residence: the central salon now has a real ocean-terrace door, the elevated west suite gains a supported guarded terrace, and the covered ocean terrace gains paired bronze privacy/shade screens.
